response.rationale: The vignette describes a patient with progressive gait disturbance, rigid-akinetic syndrome, emotional lability, and supratentorial white matter hyperintensity on T2/FLAIR sequences, which are all supportive of Progressive Supranuclear Palsy. The absence of contrast enhancement on T1 postgadolinium images further supports this diagnosis. While Multiple System Atrophy (D1) is also supported by some features, the presence of emotional lability and the specific MRI findings make Progressive Supranuclear Palsy a slightly better fit.
